Model × Dataset

The solution leaderboard (ruler v1): 45 solutions in 10 families, nested family › model › config, on every task of ur5e_alone › workspace/v2: the 42 dev tasks, and the 12 holdout tasks for the 32 solutions scored there (holdout is scored only to report a finished solution, never to pick one). A task's cell is its tool_track_rms_mm from the solution's scorecard: the RMS tool error over the samples where the target moves. Unfold a column to its speeds, task kinds and tasks; click a task's cell to open its run.

Beside it, every other measured dataset in this repo is its own column group marked off-ruler (7 groups, 2906 task results: conveyor cycle · 30 picks, workspace/v2 at speeds ×0.1…×1.0, on the upright, portal and loaded UR5e). Off-ruler columns are evidence: never pooled with the ruler's dev or holdout, never what the sort ranks on. The rail's (columns) filters pick which columns you compare: Ruler, Dataset, Split, Speed fraction, Task kind.

Roll-up, in plain words: a solution's score on a dataset is the median of its per-task numbers (that median is the objective); a folded row (a model, a family) is the median of the rows under it, one vote per row; a deployment is the plain average of its datasets' scores, every dataset counted once, and dev and holdout are never pooled; a deployment ranks only the rows scored on every one of its datasets, and a speed group the plain average of its one dataset per speed. Ruler v1 has one dataset at one speed, so the ur5e_alone · dev column is each solution's objective, and the Leaderboard ranks on it. The Roll up buttons over the grid switch the method (Median, Mean, Best, Rank, Count) and the grid says the rule it is using in words.

How the rows, the views and the links are made

Rows nest family › model › config, read from the solution's id and meta.json: the family is the id's pN root, named with the first two phrases of that root's own change ("P5 · model + Coulomb at plan time, board PD"); the model is the id's first segment (p5s), the config the rest (pass3; "as built" when there is none). A solution tagged ablation is in the family Ablations, its model its ablation kind; ablations are never ranked: the Leaderboard leaves them out, and the Pivot, which ranks nothing, draws them.

Three tables of the same rows (data-ui's leaderboard pivot, CONTRACT §57): Leaderboard (the default) ranks the solutions on the dev deployment, tints each cell by its rank in its column, and puts a picture of each task's target tool path over its column; the 30 ablations are left out. Pivot is the bare pivot with every row and column open, the ablations drawn but never ranked. Rows is every task result. In both pivots a column group folds into one roll-up column that says its method and count; the Metric control switches the number (tool tracking RMS or max, stop error, full-trajectory RMS, gates passed), and the left panel filters the columns (ruler, dataset, split, speed, task kind) and the rows (family, model, admissible). Then the charts over the same numbers (CONTRACT §58): Ranks ranks the solutions on every dev task (mean rank, Friedman's test and the Nemenyi critical difference; ablations listed, never ranked), and the Bars presets draw the medians as bars per task kind, a 95 % interval per config on one task kind, a violin per model over the tasks, and every bar as a ratio of p1's on a log scale.

A cell over one task result opens its run: in the Trajectory Comparison for the solutions saved on every dev task, in the landing page's player for those saved on one task per kind, else the task's Comparison (this run is not saved, only its score); a holdout task has no saved run, so its cell opens the records behind it, as every cell over several does; so does an off-ruler cell (only its scores are kept). Each task result's Opens says which.

Where the off-ruler rows come from: the speed study (experiments/ur5e_speed_sweep/study.json: 5 solutions × 42 dev tasks × speeds 0.1…1.0, the moving-sample tool RMS only); goal G1's sweep (goals/G1-runs/, the files goals/G1-ur5e-tracking-evidence.json names by sha256: the mount-aware controller on the 42 dev and 12 holdout upright tasks and the portal conveyor cycle at 0.1…1.0); the conveyor baseline (experiments/conveyor_cycle/parent-results.json: the unchanged controller on the conveyor cycle at 0.1…1.0); W3's loaded check (experiments/w3_loaded_ur5e_2f85/results.json: a UR5e carrying a Robotiq 2F-85 and an object; its bare cases are the scorecards bit for bit, so they are not repeated).
